This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
Help Leonard Hayes (leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co, CEO of HarmonyGames, which is shutting down) review his email history with former employees and contractors who hold stock options. The constraints are quoted verbatim: "Use ONLY read-only tools (mcp__hg__gmail_* search/get/list with user_email="leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co"). Do NOT send, draft, modify or delete anything. Current date: 2026-02-14."

Gmail search is fuzzy, so every hit must be checked: confirm the exact address appears in From/To/Cc using gmail_get_messages_batch with format="metadata" and metadata_headers ["From","To","Cc","Subject","Date"]. Read bodies with gmail_get_message or gmail_get_thread (format full). Large results are saved to a file that can be parsed with Bash/python; bodies are base64url in payload.body.data or in the parts.

Holders (addresses exactly as given):
1. ENG-2450 [PERSON_NAME_0043]: PERSON_2361_EMAIL (ES-1; termination letter 2026-02-11)
2. ENG-2452 Calvin Price: [EMAIL_0801] (ES-3; asked for extra weeks on the exercise window; Carta extension forwarded 2026-02-03, thread 1856121753612004097)
3. ENG-2453 Claire Morgan: PERSON_2360_EMAIL (ES-4; termination notice 2026-02-11)
4. ENG-2456 Marcus Bennett: marcus.bennett@harmonygames.co (ES-7; letter 2026-02-11)
5. ENG-2457 [PERSON_NAME_0068]: PERSON_3140_EMAIL (ES-12; 2026-02-11 letter bounced)
6. ENG-2458 Martin Walsh: PERSON_4363_EMAIL (ES-13; letter 2026-02-11)
7. ENG-2459 [PERSON_NAME_0051]: PERSON_2684_EMAIL (ES-14)
8. ENG-2460 "Brian Foster" (Carta name Omer [0093]): PERSON_4243_EMAIL (ES-15; letter 2026-02-11)
9. ENG-2463 Oliver Brooks ([0022]): PERSON_1174_EMAIL (ES-18)
10. ENG-2462 [PERSON_NAME_0038]: PERSON_2314_EMAIL (ES-17)
11. ENG-2461 cameron: cameron@harmonygames.co (ES-16)

For each holder, report:
- (a) Threads since 2025-09-01 that involve the exact address: date, subject, from/to/cc, gist.
- (b) Whether Leonard, Robert (robert@harmonygames.co) or Arthur Blake (arthur.blake@harmonygames.co) sent them a written message directly about the company closing, and whether it was delivered. Check for bounce messages ("Delivery Status Notification" / "Address not found") that reference the address. Give the date and a quote.
- (c) Whether the holder ever (any date) asked a question about their options or equity that went unanswered. Quote it verbatim with the date, and say whether and when it was answered. This includes thread 1789011705438137160.
- (d) Any reply to the Feb 11 2026 termination letters.

Output: a structured factual report with thread IDs and quotes, under about 1500 words.

- gmail_search_messages (fuzzy), gmail_get_messages_batch (metadata verification), gmail_get_thread and gmail_get_message (full bodies).

- Base64url body decoding via Bash/python if a result is saved to a file.

- None created or edited. No files written.

4. Errors and fixes:
- None so far.

  - Leonard's messages in late 2025: 1847220270416737293 (<CAPBs_a53DfuOTL=yinuOTXZJZR1h0Av=rSDgZikn9E3tRPeThA@mail.gmail.com>) and 1847443396264475348 (<CAPBs_a6=xbzzzb9+uBsYYzF2LFaUH9LUbpgHB1EwYv2Y8jCCWA@mail.gmail.com>).
  - Probable newsletters: 1850434252057473435, 1849800470787894468, 1849155897308448073, 1847887713399687716, 1846603044261815294, 1845964192004713118, 1845272802921531572. Also 1846180658188929017 (smartglocalwallet).

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
Help Leonard Hayes (leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co, CEO of HarmonyGames, which is shutting down) review email history with company stock/option holders.

Constraints, to be kept verbatim:
- "Use ONLY read-only tools (mcp__hg__gmail_* search/get/list tools with user_email="leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co"). Do NOT send, draft, modify or delete anything."
- Current date: 2026-02-14.
- Gmail search is fuzzy. I MUST verify the exact address appears in From/To/Cc using gmail_get_messages_batch format="metadata", metadata_headers ["From","To","Cc","Subject","Date"].
- Read bodies with gmail_get_message / gmail_get_thread (format full). Big results are saved to a file I can parse with Bash/python; bodies are base64url in payload.body.data or parts.

Holders to review (addresses exactly as given):
1. ENG-2444 Patrick Lewis – patrick@harmonygames.co (25,432 shares).
2. ENG-2446 "PERSON_3941_NAME [PERSON_NAME_0127]" – PERSON_3941_EMAIL (31,536 shares, plus option grant ES-11).
   - Robert emailed this address on 2026-02-12 saying "we're closing the company" (thread 1773963101399472184).
3. ENG-2447 Husnu Matthew Collins – matthew.collins@harmonygames.co (86,470 shares; former independent director; preferred cert SSP-10 plus option grant ES-9).
   - Leonard emailed "Husnu Akin <PERSON_8862_EMAIL>" on 2026-02-12, subject "Harmony", about shutting down.
   - Check whether that is the same person and whether it bounced.
4. ENG-2448 TOR Capital Limited – PERSON_5275_EMAIL (50,865 preferred, cert SSP-11).
5. ENG-2438/2439 Griffin Gaming Partners II, L.P. and Side Fund – partner email PERSON_4337_EMAIL.
   - Only check for any question from Griffin about their holding that was never answered.
   - Threads to check: 1856675475513544349 "Combo Fighter Data and Shut-Down" (Feb 9-12 2026), 1855133803855213163, 1851862199571842440, 1851170758917473770.

    ACTION BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF Harmony Games Inc                                  .




                                                                           November 10, 2023

   The undersigned, constituting all of the members of the Board of Directors of (the ?Board?) of Harmony

Games Inc, a Delaware corporation (the ?Company?), pursuant to Section 141(f) of the Delaware General


Corporation Law and the Bylaws of the Company, do hereby adopt the following resolutions by unanimous
written consent effective as of the latest date set forth on the signature page hereto:


                                                                               Option Grants


   WHEREAS, the Board deems it appropriate at this time to grant options under the Company’s 2023 Stock
Plan (the “Plan”);


   WHEREAS, the Board intends that such options have an exercise price per share equal to the fair market
value per share of the Company’s Common Stock on this date;


   WHEREAS, the Board previously determined that a valuation firm independent of the Company should be
retained to value the Company’s Common Stock, considered a variety of valuation firms, evaluated their
credentials, reputation, availability, cost and other criteria, and selected the Carta                  Valuations LLC (the

“Valuation Firm”) to perform the appraisal;


   WHEREAS, the Board has received, reviewed and discussed a written report issued by the Valuation Firm,
which concludes that the Company’s Common Stock has a value of $0.16 per share, as of August 21, 2023;
and


   WHEREAS, the Board has determined that the Valuation Firm is independent of the Company, that the
Valuation Firm’s report was completed less than 12 months ago and that no developments material to the
fair market value of the Company’s Common Stock have occurred since the date of such report;


   NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Board hereby determines, in reliance on the Valuation Firm’s
written report, that the current fair market value per share of the Company’s Common Stock is $0.16;


   RESOLVED FURTHER, that each individual named in Exhibit A attached here to be, and such individual
hereby is, granted an option under the Plan to acquire up to the number of shares of the Company’s
Common Stock indicated next to such individual’s name in Exhibit A. Such option shall have an exercise
price per share equal to $0.16. Such option shall be an incentive stock option under the federal tax laws or
a nonstatutory stock option, as provided in Exhibit A. Such option shall have a term of 10 years from this
date, subject to earlier expiration upon the termination of the optionee’s service with the Company. Such
option shall be evidenced by one of the forms of Stock Option Agreement approved by the Board, except
as otherwise provided in Exhibit A;


   RESOLVED FURTHER, that the shares subject to each option hereby granted shall vest as provided in
Exhibit A: one‑quarter of such shares shall vest when the optionee completes 12 months of continuous
service after the “vesting commencement date” (as specified for the optionee in Exhibit A), and 1/24th and
1/48th respectively, as outlined in Exhibit A, of such shares shall vest when the optionee completes each
month of continuous service thereafter.


   RESOLVED FURTHER, that the shares purchased under each option hereby granted shall be subject to
the Company’s right of first refusal, exercisable in the event that the optionee proposes to sell or otherwise
transfer such shares prior to the initial public offering of the Company’s Common Stock. The terms
pursuant to which such shares may be repurchased by the Company under such right of first refusal shall
be substantially as set forth inapplicable form of Stock Option Agreement; and
       FINALLY RESOLVED, that each officer of the Company be, and each such officer hereby is, authorized and
directed to take all action and to prepare, execute and deliver all documents that such officer deems
necessary or advisable to carry out the intent of these resolutions
and evidence the stock option grants hereby made, including (without limitation) the appropriate Stock
Option Agreement for each such grant and, at the time each option is exercised, the appropriate stock
certificate evidencing the purchased shares of Common Stock.

- Read bodies with gmail_get_message or gmail_get_thread (format full).

2. ENG-2446 "PERSON_3941_NAME [PERSON_NAME_0127]" – PERSON_3941_EMAIL (31,536 shares, plus option grant ES-11).

5. ENG-2438/2439 Griffin Gaming Partners II, L.P. and Side Fund – PERSON_4337_EMAIL.
   - Only check for any unanswered Griffin question about their holding.
   - Threads to check: 1856675475513544349, 1855133803855213163, 1851862199571842440, 1851170758917473770.
   - Also report the full content of thread 1856675475513544349.

For each holder, report:
- (a) Threads with the exact address: date, subject, from/to/cc, one-line gist. Focus on investment, stock, options and Carta topics, and on 2025-2026.
- (b) Whether Leonard, Robert (robert@harmonygames.co) or Arthur Blake (arthur.blake@harmonygames.co) sent them a written closing/shutdown message that was delivered (check for bounces). Give the date and a quote.
- (c) Any unanswered holding question, quoted verbatim with its date, and whether it was answered later.
- (d) Family or relationship links to other holders.

The final answer is a plain-text structured report with thread IDs and quotes, under about 1500 words. No .md files. Do not duplicate the background agents a7f2d1a88ca43a375 or a4f800ce85616af0b; they are still running, so do not spawn duplicates.

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1769892718.932069\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Simple improvement: Upgrade-adjusted difficulty multiplier (plus a tiny \\u201cskill\\u201d correction)\\nKeep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player\\u2019s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses \\u201cahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.\\u201d\\n1) Compute an upgrade power score\\nUse what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. That alone will tell you if upgrade variance is the real driver.\", \"channel\": \"C09UHHN6PFZ\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1769885600.421359\"}, {\"ts\": \"1769094763.126809\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Hey guys, I won't be able to join today's meeting, I have a doctor's appointment and some lab exams. Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. Keep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player’s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses “ahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.”
1) Compute an upgrade power score
Use what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.
• `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`
(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)
2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level
You need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:
design intent (a table), or
• median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).
3) Convert “ahead/behind” into a difficulty multiplier
• `delta = U - E[level]`
• `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`
Where `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).
Example using your comment “3 to 4 levels ahead”: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into “need to think” without nuking average players.
4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket “skill” correction
This keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.
Define `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:
• attempts per level
• time to clear
• waves reached at death (if you have it)
• number of refreshes (if relevant)
Bucket it:
• *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears
• *Average*: middle
• *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears
Then:
• `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`
Final:
• `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)
5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only
Do not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create “I have to rebuild now” moments.
Good candidates:
• enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)
• enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)
• obstacle density or obstacle removal cost
• shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)
Example:
• `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`
• `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`
(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)
A/B test design
*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.
*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).
Primary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):
• level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)
• time per level and “rebuild events” frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)
• D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)

• `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your “spender/optimizer” proxy)
• `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)
• `delta <= -2` (behind curve)

• ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that’s your target)
• average players stay near current difficulty
• weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)

1. I ingested your chapter win rate CSV and generated a per-chapter target curve and parameter plan. You can open and review it in the table I just shared. I also saved a machine-readable file:
2.  <sandbox:/mnt/data/domino_difficulty_plan.csv|Download the CSV>
What is inside for each chapter:
• target_win_rate: linear ramp from 0.95 down to 0.35 by chapter 40, clamped at 0.35 after 40.
• delta_to_target_pp: difference in percentage points vs your current average.
• pity_scalar: multiply your base pity probabilities by this scalar, 1.20 at the easiest chapters trending to 0.60 at the hardest.
• adaptive_scalar_pos: multiplier for positive AdaptivePityRule adjustments, 1.50 at easy chapters trending to 0.75 at hard.
• adaptive_scalar_neg: reciprocal to amplify negative adjustments as chapters get harder.
• hand_tiles_delta: integer offset to starting hand tiles, from +1 early to −3 in late game, subject to your minimum of 5.
• unique_symbols_delta: integer offset to unique symbol count, from 0 early to +2 late.
1. Wire-up in code
A. Chapter profiles
 Create a lightweight profile map keyed by chapter that you load from the CSV above at boot or from a baked asset.
```public sealed class ChapterDifficultyProfile {
    public int Chapter;
    public float TargetWinRate;        // 0..1
    public float PityScalar;           // e.g., 1.20 easy → 0.60 hard
    public float AdaptiveScalarPos;    // e.g., 1.50 easy → 0.75 hard
    public float AdaptiveScalarNeg;    // 1 / AdaptiveScalarPos
    public int HandTilesDelta;         // e.g., +1 → −3, apply with min 5 guard
    public int UniqueSymbolsDelta;     // e.g., 0 → +2
}```
B. Apply pity scaling without changing arrays by hand
 Wrap your pity rates once per level load.
```static float[] ScalePityRates(float[] baseRates, float scalar) {
    // Clamp to [0,1], keep cumulative nondecreasing if you transform cumulative arrays.
    var scaled = new float[baseRates.Length];
    for (int i = 0; i < baseRates.Length; i++) scaled[i] = MathF.Min(1f, MathF.Max(0f, baseRates[i] * scalar));
    // Optional: enforce monotonic nondecreasing
    for (int i = 1; i < scaled.Length; i++) scaled[i] = MathF.Max(scaled[i], scaled[i - 1]);
    return scaled;
}```
Use per-chapter scalar:
```var prof = DifficultyProfiles.GetForChapter(chapter);
var pityRules = new[]{
    new PityMechanicRatesRule(ScalePityRates(new float[]{0.10f,0.20f,0.41f,0.55f,1.0f}, prof.PityScalar), 1),
    new PityMechanicRatesRule(ScalePityRates(new float[]{0.05f,0.10f,0.21f,0.55f,1.0f}, prof.PityScalar), 3),
    new PityMechanicRatesRule(ScalePityRates(new float[]{0.02f,0.05f,0.20f,0.30f,0.35f,0.60f}, prof.PityScalar), 5),
    new PityMechanicRatesRule(ScalePityRates(new float[]{0.02f,0.04f,0.06f,0.10f,0.15f,0.30f}, prof.PityScalar), 7),
};```
C. Scale adaptive pity without rewriting rules
 Multiply your positive and negative RateAdjustment values at build time.
```static AdaptivePityRule Scale(AdaptivePityRule r, float pos, float neg) {
    var k = r.RateAdjustment >= 0 ? pos : neg;
    return new AdaptivePityRule(r.PityRuleType, r.Min, r.Max, r.RateAdjustment * k);
}

var prof = DifficultyProfiles.GetForChapter(chapter);
var adaptive = AdaptivePityRule.DefaultRules
    .Select(r => Scale(r, prof.AdaptiveScalarPos, prof.AdaptiveScalarNeg))
    .ToArray();```
D. Apply hand tiles and unique symbols deltas
 Respect your min hand tile guard of 5.
```// Before level start
handTiles = Math.Max(5, handTiles + prof.HandTilesDelta);
uniqueSymbols = Math.Max(3, uniqueSymbols + prof.UniqueSymbolsDelta); // keep a sensible floor```
E. Keep your existing player bucketing
 Your bucketing rules already trim tiles for top players. Leave them as is, since chapter-level deltas apply first and bucketing remains a per-player overlay.
1. Rollout sequence
• Phase 1: Enable pity_scalar only. Ship, collect per-chapter win rates for 3 to 5 days. Confirm the curve trends down toward the targets.
• Phase 2: Add adaptive_scalar_pos and adaptive_scalar_neg scaling. Verify session length and last-move drama do not regress.
• Phase 3: Enable hand_tiles_delta and unique_symbols_delta, with A/B guardrails on early economy and booster attach.
2. Verification metrics to watch
• Win rate by chapter and by bucket vs target_win_rate.
• Attempts per win and average moves remaining at win, both should trend up with chapter.
• Booster attach rates, do not allow pay-to-pass spikes to mask overtuned late chapters.
• Rage quit percent and 1-day return rate by chapter entry.
The attached CSV is ready to plug in. In our last build everything passed, yet a single feature change on the client side took down *all* client‑server communication. That should never be possible. The API contract must be designed so that the backend remains stable even when the client misbehaves or drifts ahead.
Here is the principle: *the server owns the truth and must be resilient to any bad or unexpected payload the client sends.* That means:
*Strict validation with graceful fallback*
 Parse every request defensively. Reject or sanitize unknown fields but still return a well‑formed error payload so the client can recover.
*Versioning and feature flags*
 Never repurpose an existing field. Introduce new versions or gated features so older clients keep working.
*Default values and sensible degradation*
 When optional data is missing or malformed, fall back to safe defaults rather than aborting the whole pipeline.
*Timeouts and circuit breakers*
 If the client hangs or floods with retries, isolate the failure so it does not cascade to other users.
*Comprehensive integration tests*
 Simulate skewed or corrupted client requests in CI to prove the backend can still respond correctly.
*Monitoring and alerting*
 Surface spikes in 4xx/5xx responses quickly so we can roll back or hot‑patch without a full outage.
The takeaway: we can never assume clients are perfect, especially on mobile where hotfixes roll out at different times. This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
The user is Leonard Hayes, co-founder of HarmonyGames, which is winding down. Current date is 2026-02-14 (Feb 14, 2026).

He asked me to complete the stockholder/option-holder close-out exactly as his Linear "Holder records" project and his Google Doc "Stockholder close-out notes" lay it out. That means:
- **Holder sheet:** finish his existing draft sheet in the close-out folder rather than starting a new one.
- **Investor letter:** a Google Doc in the close-out folder, worked up from his Feb 9 investor email draft in #winddown, using the sections from the "Harmony Games February 26 Update" outline.
- **Holder messages:** saved as Gmail drafts only. They must NOT be sent; Leonard reads and sends each one himself.
- **Linear issues:** set states and add comments.
- **Heads-up to Griffin:** sent.
- **Reply in #winddown:** sent.
- **Reply to KPMG's audit request (from Feb 13):** sent.

He said, verbatim: "Send the replies yourself, no need to check with me; only the holder messages wait for me."

Rules from the close-out notes:
- One note per investor, sent individually, not one mail to everyone.
- The sheet comes first. Share the sheet and the letter with Robert (robert@harmonygames.co). Per a #winddown thread reply, the sheet also goes to Arthur Blake (arthur.blake@harmonygames.co).
- Notes should be ready for Leonard by Tuesday.
- Everything goes in the close-out folder (d_601064334a0b493022fe83), NOT the Wind Down folder.
- Griffin heads-up: reply-all on their partner's own "Board position" mail from Feb 12, asking for their vote as preferred holders on the dissolution. Send only once the sheet is done.
- When the sheet is ready, reply under Leonard's list in #winddown and say who goes first.
- Carta is the record, over any date in the letters. If a line's last day has passed, it holds nothing.
- One row per issue; counts go by rows; at most one note per person. The three founders get no row, only the totals.
- "Told" means a written message about the closing, sent to them directly and delivered, from Leonard, Robert or Arthur. A post in a channel doesn't count. For a fund, the message must reach its partner.
- Everyone still holding something gets what they're owed: news of the closing if not yet told, and their last day if they have one. Whoever's last day comes first goes first.
- Each note says what the holder holds, and answers any question about their holding that was never answered.
- Messages go to the email on each holder's Linear issue.
- Sheet labels: Nothing, Already told, Closing, Last day, Closing and last day.
- From the #winddown thread: for angel families, one note to whoever has always handled it for the family covers the other family lines. Those lines need no note of their own, are marked "Covered" in place of a label, and are counted that way. That one note says what each family member holds.

Rules from the Linear project:
- After the sheet is done, set states: Canceled where the line holds nothing; Todo where its own note is waiting for Leonard; Done where it isn't.
- On every issue with no note of its own (Canceled included), add a comment saying why.
- Leonard passes the sheet to Sunset himself.
- Send KPMG's confirmation as a reply-all once the sheet is done.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

**Tools in use:**
- MCP tools: Gmail, Google Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides, Linear, Slack, Snowflake.
- Gmail search is fuzzy for address tokens. Precise `from:ADDR OR to:ADDR` queries do work. Addresses written in brackets (Calvin's "[EMAIL_0801]") return no results.
- Gmail `format=full` is limited to 10 messages per batch. Large results get saved to files and decoded with a python script at `/tmp/w/msgs.py`, which base64url-decodes bodies. A helper `/tmp/w/clean.sh` strips boilerplate.
- `pdftotext` works on attachments saved to `/tmp/w/`.

**Names are anonymized inconsistently.** Mappings confirmed so far:
- ENG-2460 "Brian Foster" = Carta "Ömer [0093]"; email PERSON_4243_EMAIL; option grant ES-15.
- ENG-2454 [0612] = "Douglas".
- ENG-2447 "Husnu Matthew Collins": former independent director, also called "Husnu Akin", personal address PERSON_8862_EMAIL.
- Julia Lawson is likely [0043] (ENG-2450).
- Claire Morgan is EMPLOYEE_0009 on Slack.

Each issue has two comments: its number on the Nov 2024 owner list, and the date of the last email with that address before Feb. Issue → email:

import json,base64,sys,re
def dec(s):
    s=s.replace('-','+').replace('_','/'); return base64.b64decode(s+'='*(-len(s)%4)).decode(errors='replace')
def walk(p):
    out=[]
    if p.get('body',{}).get('data') and p.get('mimeType','').startswith('text/plain'): out.append(dec(p['body']['data']))
    for c in p.get('parts',[]) or []: out+=walk(c)
    if not out and p.get('body',{}).get('data'): out.append(dec(p['body']['data']))
    return out
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    d=json.load(open(f)); d=json.loads(d['result']) if 'result' in d else d
    ms=d.get('messages',[d])
    for m in ms:
        h={x['name']:x['value'] for x in m.get('payload',{}).get('headers',[])}
        print('###',m['id'][:90]); print('Date:',h.get('Date'),'| From:',h.get('From'),'| To:',h.get('To'),'| Cc:',h.get('Cc'),'| Subj:',h.get('Subject'), '| labels', m.get('labelIds'))
        body='\n'.join(walk(m.get('payload',{})))
        body=body.split('Learn more about Carta')[0]
        print(body.strip()[:4000]); print()

HarmonyGames – February 2026 Update to Our Investors

Hi everyone,

I'm writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down HarmonyGames. I want you to hear it from me directly, with as much clarity as I can give on what happened, where things stand and what it means for you.

1. What happened

What we did and what we learned. Over the last two and a half years we built and shipped three games: Domino Delights, Zombie Match 3D and Combo Fighter. Each taught us a great deal about casual puzzle players, live operations and user acquisition, and the team did excellent work. None of them reached the retention and monetization we needed to fund the next stage of growth.

Why we are closing. The business has been under financial strain since mid-2025. Despite cutting costs and exploring financing and partnership options, we were not able to secure new capital, and our runway fell below one month. On February 9, 2026 the board decided that an orderly wind-down is the most responsible path for our investors, our team and our partners.

2. Where things stand

Holders. Our cap table, per Carta (our record) as of today: 6,000,000 shares of common stock held by the three founders; 3,051,879 shares of Series Seed Preferred, of which Griffin Gaming Partners II and its Side Fund hold 2,746,693 and our angel investors hold 305,186; and 164,114 vested options still outstanding. Option lines whose post-termination exercise window has passed have lapsed and hold nothing.

Board, process and who is running the close. The board is now Leonard Hayes and Robert; Griffin's director resigned from the board on February 12. We have engaged Sunset to run the formal dissolution, and the board will be asking the Series Seed Preferred holders for their vote on the dissolution. Formal notices will follow separately from Sunset. We are closing obligations in an orderly way: paying down our bank debt and closing the company credit card, terminating vendor contracts, completing employee terminations, and archiving company systems once the remaining data has been extracted.

3. What it means for you

Distributions. We do not expect any distribution to stockholders. The company's remaining assets are going to its creditors and the costs of an orderly dissolution, and the Series Seed Preferred liquidation preference sits ahead of common stock. If that changes in the course of the dissolution, Sunset will tell you.

Tax papers. Any final tax forms will be issued as part of the dissolution. Please talk to your own tax adviser about how to treat your investment; this letter is not tax advice.

Your options. If you hold options, the vested part can still be exercised until the last day shown in your Carta account (your post-termination exercise window). Given that no distribution is expected, we do not recommend exercising, and you do not need to do anything. Options not exercised by their last day simply lapse.

4. What happens to the games and the IP

We are sunsetting our live games and winding down the related services. We agreed a data licensing deal for $22,500 under which the buyer licenses the company's data; HarmonyGames keeps ownership of all of its IP. The board will continue to evaluate what, if anything, can be done with the remaining IP during the dissolution.

5. Thank you

Thank you for believing in us, for your money, your time and your advice. I'm deeply grateful, and I'm sorry we couldn't build the outcome we all hoped for. If you'd like to talk 1:1, please reply and I'll set up a time.

Thank you,
Leonard

Hi,

A quick heads-up: we are moving ahead with dissolving HarmonyGames, with Sunset running the formal process. As holders of Series Seed Preferred (Griffin Gaming Partners II: 2,662,255 shares; Side Fund: 84,438 shares, together about 90% of the preferred), Griffin's vote is needed to approve the dissolution. Could you please confirm that Griffin will vote in favor of it as preferred holders? The formal consent and notices will come through Sunset.

Thank you again for all your support.

Best,
Leonard

Hi,

Here is the confirmation you requested, as of December 31, 2025, per Carta (our capitalization record).

1. Shares outstanding by class
- Common stock: 6,000,000
- Series Seed Preferred: 3,051,879, of which:
  - Griffin Gaming Partners II, L.P.: 2,662,255
  - Griffin Gaming Partners II Side Fund, L.P.: 84,438
  - Other Series Seed holders: 305,186

2. Options outstanding at December 31, 2025, by line (effective dates as in Carta)
Lines terminated on or before December 31, 2025 count only what had vested by their termination date; lines whose post-termination exercise window had already lapsed by that date are excluded (ES-2, last day Nov 1, 2024; ES-6, last day Jul 16, 2025).
- ES-1 – [0043]: 17,802 (terminated Dec 31, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-3 – Calvin Price: 4,408 (terminated Oct 24, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-4 – Claire Morgan: 4,450 (terminated Dec 31, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-5 – [0612]: 5,298 (terminated Oct 24, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-7 – Marcus Bennett: 22,889 (in service at Dec 31, 2025)
- ES-8 – [0089]: 30,518 (advisor)
- ES-9 – Husnu Matthew Collins: 61,038 (advisor)
- ES-10 – PERSON_1287_NAME: 6,104 (advisor)
- ES-11 – PERSON_3941_NAME: 6,104 (advisor)
- ES-12 – [0068]: 16,277 (in service at Dec 31, 2025)
- ES-13 – Martin Walsh: 3,866 (in service at Dec 31, 2025)
- ES-14 – [0051]: 1,530 (terminated Nov 21, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-15 – Brian Foster: 3,391 (terminated Dec 31, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-16 – cameron: 10,384 (terminated Oct 24, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-17 – [0038]: 34,439 (terminated Oct 24, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-18 – [0022]: 15,259 (in service at Dec 31, 2025)
Total options outstanding: 243,757

3. Shares and options together (fully diluted): 6,000,000 + 3,051,879 + 243,757 = 9,295,636

4. Financing and significant events since December 31, 2025
- No new financing has been raised.
- On February 9, 2026 the board decided to wind down the company. We engaged Sunset on February 12, 2026 to run the formal dissolution, and the company is winding down.
- Griffin's director resigned from the board on February 12, 2026.
- On February 12, 2026 the company signed a data licensing agreement ($22,500); the company retains ownership of all its IP.
- Option lines terminated after December 31, 2025 (ES-7, ES-12, ES-13, ES-18, terminated January 30, 2026) now count only their vested portions, and several post-termination exercise windows have since lapsed.

Please let me know if you need anything else.

Best,
Leonard

input.subject: Re: Board position
input.body:
Hi PERSON_4337_NAME,

A quick heads-up: we are moving ahead with dissolving HarmonyGames, with Sunset running the formal process. As holders of Series Seed Preferred (Griffin Gaming Partners II: 2,662,255 shares; Side Fund: 84,438 shares, together about 90% of the preferred), Griffin's vote is needed to approve the dissolution. Could you please confirm that Griffin will vote in favor of it as preferred holders? The formal consent and notices will come through Sunset.

Thank you again for all your support over the last three years.

Best,
Leonard

input.subject: RE: GRIFFIN GAMING PARTNERS 2025 Audit Request [SOURCE_ORG_0001], Inc.
input.body:
Hi,

Resending with everyone on the thread copied. Here is the confirmation you requested, as of December 31, 2025, per Carta (our capitalization record).

1. Shares outstanding by class
- Common stock: 6,000,000
- Series Seed Preferred: 3,051,879, of which:
  - Griffin Gaming Partners II, L.P.: 2,662,255
  - Griffin Gaming Partners II Side Fund, L.P.: 84,438
  - Other Series Seed holders: 305,186

2. Options outstanding at December 31, 2025, by line (effective dates as in Carta)
Lines terminated on or before December 31, 2025 count only what had vested by their termination date; lines whose post-termination exercise window had already lapsed by that date are excluded (ES-2, last day Nov 1, 2024; ES-6, last day Jul 16, 2025).
- ES-1 – [0043]: 17,802 (terminated Dec 31, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-3 – Calvin Price: 4,408 (terminated Oct 24, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-4 – Claire Morgan: 4,450 (terminated Dec 31, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-5 – [0612]: 5,298 (terminated Oct 24, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-7 – Marcus Bennett: 22,889 (in service at Dec 31, 2025)
- ES-8 – [0089]: 30,518 (advisor)
- ES-9 – Husnu Matthew Collins: 61,038 (advisor)
- ES-10 – PERSON_1287_NAME: 6,104 (advisor)
- ES-11 – PERSON_3941_NAME: 6,104 (advisor)
- ES-12 – [0068]: 16,277 (in service at Dec 31, 2025)
- ES-13 – Martin Walsh: 3,866 (in service at Dec 31, 2025)
- ES-14 – [0051]: 1,530 (terminated Nov 21, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-15 – Brian Foster: 3,391 (terminated Dec 31, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-16 – cameron: 10,384 (terminated Oct 24, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-17 – [0038]: 34,439 (terminated Oct 24, 2025; vested portion)
- ES-18 – [0022]: 15,259 (in service at Dec 31, 2025)
Total options outstanding: 243,757

3. Shares and options together (fully diluted): 6,000,000 + 3,051,879 + 243,757 = 9,295,636

4. Financing and significant events since December 31, 2025
- No new financing has been raised.
- On February 9, 2026 the board decided to wind down the company. We engaged Sunset on February 12, 2026 to run the formal dissolution, and the company is winding down.
- Griffin's director resigned from the board on February 12, 2026.
- On February 12, 2026 the company signed a data licensing agreement ($22,500); the company retains ownership of all its IP.
- Option lines terminated after December 31, 2025 (ES-7, ES-12, ES-13, ES-18, terminated January 30, 2026) now count only their vested portions, and several post-termination exercise windows have since lapsed.

Please let me know if you need anything else.

Best,
Leonard

content.text:
The close-out is finished, with one slip on my side: the two "reply-all" emails first went out without their Cc lists. I resent both in the same threads to everyone, so Robert got the Griffin heads-up twice and the main KPMG contact got the audit reply twice. Your 15 holder messages are saved as Gmail drafts and nothing has been sent to any holder.

**Holder sheet.** I finished your "Holder list (draft)" in the close-out folder and shared it with Robert and Arthur. It has one row per Linear issue (26 rows) and follows Carta. It also has the totals, the count of rows by label, the directors and who holds the preferred vote, which is what Sunset asked for.

| Label | Rows |
|---|---|
| Closing and last day | 4 |
| Last day | 5 |
| Closing | 6 |
| Covered | 2 |
| Already told | 4 |
| Nothing | 5 |

- **Shares and options today:** 6,000,000 common, 3,051,879 Series Seed Preferred (Griffin holds 2,746,693 of that) and 164,114 vested options still live, for 9,215,993 in total.
- **Families:** the Disli brothers are the only angel family. Their note goes to issue 2443, who has always handled it, and lists all three holdings. Patrick (2444) and 2445 are marked Covered.
- **Nothing:** five people's options lapsed when their last day passed. That includes the 127,162 shown on the Nov 2024 list for 2462, which was an option grant that has now lapsed.

**Holder drafts, in sending order:**
1. Calvin – last day Feb 20.
2. [0051] – last day Feb 21.
3. Mar 31 last days: 2450, Claire, Brian.
4. Apr 30 last days: Marcus, [0068], Martin, [0022].
5. No last day: [0089], Arthur, [4468], the Disli family, TOR, and 2449.

Claire's draft also answers the equity question you hadn't replied to in your Feb 12 Slack chat: she doesn't need to do anything.

**Before you send:**
- **[0068]:** your Feb 11 letter to [0068] bounced, and the draft uses the same address because it's the one on the Linear issue. Please check the address first.
- **Calvin:** the address on his Linear issue is a placeholder, "[EMAIL_0801]", so his draft needs a real address before you send it Monday.
- **Exercise prices:** I left them out for [0068], Martin and [0051], because I couldn't find them in the records I checked.
- **Disli family:** I don't have the third brother's name, so the draft says "your other brother". Fill in his name before sending.

**Investor letter:** a new Doc in the close-out folder, built from your Feb 9 #winddown draft and laid out in the outline's five sections. Holder numbers come from Carta, not the Nov 2024 list. It's shared with Robert.

**Linear:** 15 issues are Todo, the 4 Already told and 2 Covered are Done, and the 5 Nothing are Canceled. Each of the 11 issues without its own note has a comment saying why.

**Sent:**
- **Griffin heads-up:** in the "Board position" thread, to their partner with Robert, Arthur and PERSON_2847 copied, asking for Griffin's vote as preferred holders on the dissolution.
- **KPMG:** to everyone on the thread. It gives the Dec 31, 2025 figures: 243,757 options outstanding and 9,295,636 shares and options together, plus a note that there's no new financing and the company is winding down.
- **#winddown:** a reply under your list saying the sheet is done and Calvin goes first, then [0051].

Passing the sheet to Sunset is still with you.
